routes.label: Find a divisor of every candidate

question:
For any integer \(n\) greater than \(1,\) the number of prime numbers greater than \(n!+1\) and less than \(n!+n\) is:

Here \(n!=1\cdot2\cdots(n-1)n.\)
solution:
For \(n=2\), the interval is strictly between \(3\) and \(4\), so it contains no integers.

Now suppose \(n\ge3\). Every integer strictly between \(n!+1\) and \(n!+n\) has the form
\[
n!+k,\qquad 2\le k\le n-1.
\]
The useful observation is that \(k\) is one of the factors in \(n!=1\cdot2\cdots n\). Therefore \(n!/k\) is a positive integer, and
\[
n!+k=k\left(\frac{n!}{k}+1\right).
\]
Here \(k\ge2\), and the other factor is also at least \(2\). Thus every candidate is composite. This covers every integer in the open interval, so there are \(\boxed{0}\) primes, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
